record.paper_title: THE LYAPIN’S NOTEBOOK: A COLLECTION OF UNSOLVED PROBLEMS IN SEMIGROUP THEORY
record.original_question: Describe all varieties of ordered semigroups that have covers in the lattice of ordered-semigroup varieties.

evidence.quote:
Problem 2.8. (E.S. Lyapin) Describe all varieties of ordered semigroups that have covers in the
lattice of varieties of ordered semigroups.
Some such varieties are described in works [18], [19]. In the lattice of varieties of ordered semi-
groups, not every variety has a cover (see [18]).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An ordered semigroup is a triple $(S,\cdot,\le)$ where $(S,\cdot)$ is a semigroup and $\le$ is a partial order on $S$ that is compatible with the multiplication, i.e., $a\le b$ implies $ca\le cb$ and $ac\le bc$ for all $a,b,c\in S$. A variety of ordered semigroups is a class of ordered semigroups defined by a set of inequalities $u\le v$ between semigroup terms, equivalently a class closed under taking ordered subsemigroups, order-preserving homomorphic images, and direct products (with componentwise order). The collection of all varieties of ordered semigroups, ordered by inclusion, forms a complete lattice $\mathcal{L}$. For two varieties $\mathcal{U}\subsetneq \mathcal{V}$ in $\mathcal{L}$, $\mathcal{V}$ is called a cover of $\mathcal{U}$ if there is no variety $\mathcal{W}$ with $\mathcal{U}\subsetneq \mathcal{W}\subsetneq \mathcal{V}$. A variety $\mathcal{U}\in\mathcal{L}$ is said to "have a cover" if there exists at least one variety $\mathcal{V}\in\mathcal{L}$ that is a cover of $\mathcal{U}$.

Problem. Give a complete description (characterization) of all varieties of ordered semigroups that have a cover in the lattice $\mathcal{L}$ of varieties of ordered semigroups.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem, attributed to E.S. Lyapin, is listed as an unsolved problem in a 2026 compilation of open problems in semigroup theory. Partial results describing some varieties having covers exist (notably work by V.A. Makaridina), and it is known that not every variety of ordered semigroups has a cover, but a full description has not been published. The problem appears to remain open.
